title: Early detection of severe fetal growth restriction using multimodal deep learning based on ultrasound and prenatal biomarkers

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Early detection of severe fetal growth restriction using multimodal deep learning based on ultrasound and prenatal biomarkers》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · S0001-p1】Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is a major pregnancy complication characterized by the failure of the fetus to reach its full growth potential. It is a leading cause of stillbirth, neonatal morbidity, neurodevelopmental disorders, and long-term metabolic and cardiovascular disease.1–3 According to international guidelines, FGR is diagnosed when estimated fetal weight (EFW) or abdominal circumference (AC) is below the 3rd percentile, or below the 10th percentile with abnormal Doppler findings.4–7 In low- and middle-income countries, the prevalence of FGR ranges from 5% to 25%, often overlapping with small-for-gestational-age (SGA) status.1,8

【Introduction · S0001-p2】Early identification of pregnancies at risk for FGR is essential for initiating preventive strategies, such as initiating low-dose aspirin before 16 weeks’ gestation in women at increased risk of preeclampsia, which may confer downstream benefits for FGR/SGA, and for guiding antenatal surveillance and delivery planning.9,10 However, current screening methods have limited sensitivity, as subtle placental dysfunctions may not be apparent until late gestation when growth deviation or abnormal Doppler findings occur.5,6,11 Therefore, there is a critical need for more accurate early prediction methods.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Early detection of severe fetal growth restriction using multimodal deep learning based on ultrasound and prenatal biomarkers》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Experiment setup · S0003-S2003-p1】All experiments were conducted on an NVIDIA RTX 4080 Super GPU with an Intel Core i9-14900KF CPU. The dataset included paired ultrasound images and clinical annotations, which were preprocessed and split into training, validation, and test sets at a 7:1:2 ratio. To ensure robustness, five-fold cross-validation was performed, and average metrics were reported across folds, including comparative and ablation experiments. The model was optimized using stochastic gradient descent (SGD) with momentum and cross-entropy loss. A learning rate scheduler was applied to improve convergence and avoid local minima. Model performance was evaluated using Precision, F1-score, Accuracy, and Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC). Interpretability was enhanced using ROC curves for threshold analysis, confusion matrices for classification alignment, and Grad-CAM heatmaps to visualize salient image regions contributing to predictions.

【Materials and methods · abstract-2-1】In this prospective study, 13,991 pregnant women were initially recruited, and after applying inclusion and exclusion criteria, 598 singleton pregnancies (299 with severe FGR and 299 controls) were analyzed. Severe FGR was diagnosed at or after 24 weeks' gestation and defined as an estimated fetal weight (EFW) or abdominal circumference (AC) below the 3rd percentile. Seven ultrasound views were collected (first-trimester crown-rump length, nuchal translucency; second-trimester head and abdominal circumference, femur length, umbilical artery S/D ratio, and amniotic fluid depth), along with maternal age and first-trimester serum markers (PAPP-A and free β-hCG, expressed as MoM). A convolutional neural network (CNN) with multi-level attention and dynamic convolution modules was trained end-to-end using stochastic gradient descent with cross-entropy loss. Model performance was evaluated with five-fold cross-validation.

Severe FGR was diagnosed at or after 24 weeks' gestation and defined as an estimated fetal weight (EFW) or abdominal circumference (AC) below the 3rd percentile. sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Early detection of severe fetal growth restriction using multimodal deep learning based on ultrasound and prenatal biomarkers》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusion · S0005-p1】This study demonstrates that a deep learning model integrating routine prenatal ultrasound images with early pregnancy biochemical markers can substantially improve the early prediction of severe FGR. The model achieved an F1-score of 0.912 and an MCC of 0.7982, outperforming ResNet-50 by +3.91% and +5.06%, respectively. By combining spatial attention mechanisms, Dynamic Convolution, and multimodal fusion, the model captures both anatomical and physiological indicators of impaired placental function. The use of standard prenatal data ensures real-world applicability, highlighting the promise of artificial intelligence to support earlier and more individualized care for at-risk pregnancies.

【Results · abstract-3-1】The integrated model achieved high predictive accuracy for severe FGR, with an AUC of approximately 0.96, accuracy of 91%, and F1-score of 0.912. Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) was 0.798. The model outperformed single-modality baselines, such as a ResNet-50 CNN trained on images alone. Ablation experiments showed that adding maternal serum biomarkers and advanced CNN modules significantly improved performance. The model demonstrated excellent discrimination between severe FGR and control cases, with high sensitivity and precision in classification.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Early detection of severe fetal growth restriction using multimodal deep learning based on ultrasound and prenatal biomarkers》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【Figure 1. · F0001】Figure 1. Flowchart of participant selection and dataset allocation. A total of 13,991 pregnant women were initially enrolled. After excluding 3,018 pregnancies due to declining participation (n = 1,158), missing outcome/follow-up data (n = 982), fetal structural or chromosomal abnormalities (n = 761), or miscarriage before 22 weeks (n = 117), 10,973 singleton pregnancies remained eligible. Among these eligible pregnancies, 299 met the study definition of severe FGR (diagnosed at or after 24 weeks’ gestation; estimated fetal weight (EFW) or abdominal circumference (AC) < 3rd percentile for gestational age). Controls (n = 299) were selected from the remaining non-FGR pregnancies and matched 1:1 by gestational age at ultrasound, defined as the gestational age at the first-trimester and second-trimester examinations. The matched dataset (n = 598) was randomly split into training, validation, and testing sets in a 7:1:2 ratio for model development and evaluation.

【Figure 2. · F0002】Figure 2. Architecture of the multi-modal FGR classification model. This model integrates ultrasound image features and clinical data for predicting FGR. The image input passes through a backbone consisting of basic blocks with dynamic convolutions, local and global attention mechanisms, and a self-attention module. The structured maternal screening variables, including maternal age, PAPP-A MoM, and β-hCG MoM, are reshaped and combined with extracted features. The concatenated features are fed into the final classifier to predict FGR or control status.

【Figure 3. · F0003】Figure 3. Ablation experiment results. Panels A–E show confusion matrices for various models: Baseline (A), Baseline + Dynamic Conv (B), Baseline + Dynamic Conv + Local_Att (C), Our (D), and Our + Clinical Data (E). Panel F presents the ROC curve comparison for these models, with AUC values indicated for each model.
